| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$50$** | **$58$** | **$62$** | **$65$** | **$70$** |
| $y$ | $10$ | $12$ | $15$ | $20$ | $17$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $5$ | $9$ | $15$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14241294/assets/a551b84a518a76b3131c86b8d884daca649bb4934368b5b970b8d8be0496e2c7.svg)

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Find  $X$ and $\mathbf{y}$ in this context.
current_example.worked_solution:
| $x_1$ | **$\color{blue}1$** | **$\color{blue}2$** | **$\color{blue}3$** | **$\color{blue}4$** | **$\color{blue}5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x_2$ | **$\color{purple}7$** | **$\color{purple}6.5$** | **$\color{purple}6$** | **$\color{purple}5$** | **$\color{purple}3$** |
| $y$ | $\color{red}1$ | $\color{red}2$ | $\color{red}5$ | $\color{red}9$ | $\color{red}15$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & 2 & 6.5 \\ 1 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5 \\ 9 \\ 15\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
